question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & 25\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

current_example.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14118729/assets/1a78dfb5270978ce1250af624fa81a3f9ef5abca2e8925155c0c023f30f0ee55.svg)

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
current_example.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14118729/assets/8ed37ebcfd63079a99b8386a107571780ffddae02914ff40c3358663c109b7d2.svg)

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=2$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+(2)=-2\,⟹\,y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=-4$ and $z=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-4)+(2)=1\,⟹\,x=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-5,$ $y=-4,$ and $z=2.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -5,-4,2 \rangle.$
